title: Tools, workflow and delivery: from brief to written decision
course_title: Remote Work & Team Collaboration: Leading Distributed Teams

say: Tools, workflow and delivery.
This is the video for module two of Remote Work and Team Collaboration.
A distributed team lives inside its tools. When files sit on personal laptops and decisions are buried in private chats, the team spends hours searching and asking.

panel.heading: Remote work goes wrong in the gaps
items: Files on personal laptops
Decisions buried in private chats
Two people each think the other owns it
Fix: one written source of truth

say: Work also falls into gaps, like two people each thinking the other owns a task.

say: The fix is a single source of truth. For each kind of information, the team agrees one place where the current version lives. Chat only points to it.

say: Think of five layers. Files and documents: edit the shared file, and never email attachments back and forth.

items: Files: edit the shared file, no attachments
Tasks: if it is not on the board, not agreed
Messaging: use threads, point to sources
Meetings: agenda before, summary after
Handbook: answer a repeated question once

You do not need every paid tool. Agree which tool does which job, and stop using the others for that job.

say: For example, Halima's programme drive had files named final report, final report 2, and FINAL final. Nobody knew which was current.
She created one top-level folder per year, then one per project.

panel.heading: Tidy a shared drive
items: One folder per year, then per project
Five fixed subfolders in each project
Name files: date, project, type, version
Share links, not attachments

say: Inside each project she fixed five subfolders, such as Admin, Plans, Field Data, Reports and Media.

panel.heading: Tidy a shared drive
items: One folder per year, then per project
Five fixed subfolders in each project
Name files: date, project, type, version
Share links, not attachments

say: She set a naming pattern: date, project code, document type, version.

panel.heading: Tidy a shared drive
items: One folder per year, then per project

say: Then she asked coordinators to share links, not attachments, on WhatsApp. Now they find the current report in seconds.

say: Put the date first, year, month, day, so files sort in date order on any device.

panel.rule: Put the date first as YYYY-MM-DD so files sort in order.

say: Shared drives hold personal data, so protect them. Turn on two-step verification for every work account.

cards.d: Turn it on for every work account, including WhatsApp, email and the drive.
Share personal data with named people only. Remove leavers' access the same day.
Fake 'document shared with you' emails steal passwords. Open the drive from your own bookmark.

say: Give the least access needed. Do not share files with personal data with anyone with the link. When someone leaves, remove their access the same day.

say: And watch for fake document shared with you emails. If unsure, open the drive from your own bookmark, not the email link.

say: Every task needs one named owner. For decisions, the DACI framework gives four roles.

panel.heading: One owner, clear decision roles
items: Driver: gets the decision made on time
Approver: the one person who decides
Contributors: a voice, not a vote
Informed: told once it is decided

say: The Driver gathers information and gets the decision made by the agreed date. The Approver is the one person who decides.

panel.heading: One owner, clear decision roles
items: Driver: gets the decision made on time
Approver: the one person who decides
Contributors: a voice, not a vote
Informed: told once it is decided

say: Contributors give expert input, a voice but not a vote. The Informed are told once it is decided.
Naming these roles ends decisions that are discussed for weeks and never made.

panel.heading: One owner, clear decision roles
items: Driver: gets the decision made on time
Approver: the one person who decides
Contributors: a voice, not a vote
Informed: told once it is decided

say: Every Friday Kemi posts a status update in the same five parts: status, done, next, blocked, and decisions needed.
This week her status is At risk, because the flyer artwork is 3 days late.
Her decision needed: print 5,000 flyers at about 45 naira each, about 225,000 naira, or 3,000 at about 55 naira each, about 165,000 naira.
She names the Driver, herself, and the Approver, Bola. She recommends 3,000, because 38 volunteers can hand out about 80 each.
Bola approves in a comment, and Kemi logs the decision with the date and the reason.
A one-hour call with eight people uses eight hours of team time, plus data costs. So first ask: could this be a document with comments?

panel.heading: Meetings that earn their time
items: Ask first: could this be a document?
Agenda 24 hours before, with pre-reads
Name roles: facilitator, note-taker
Read back actions with owners and dates
Post the summary within one working day

say: If you meet, post the agenda at least 24 hours before. Write each item as a question with the outcome you need.

say: Name a facilitator and a note-taker, and rotate them so the same person is not always taking notes.

say: End with the actions read aloud, with owners and dates. Then post a short summary within one working day.

say: People who could not attend must be able to act on it. Copy each decision into the decision log.

panel.rule: The meeting is not finished until the summary is posted.

say: To remember. Give each kind of information one home, and name files date first.
Give every task one owner and every decision one Approver.
Post a weekly update in a fixed format. Mark work At risk the moment you doubt the date. And make every meeting end with a written summary.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One home for each kind of information
Date-first file names, links not attachments
One owner per task; one Approver per decision
Weekly update: status, done, next, blocked, decide
Agenda before, written summary after
